# Result
Stable replacement: an authorization envelope plus compact universal invariants. Lower procedure may constrain or stop, never create scope. Evidence separates rule defects, procedural amplification, tool defects, and agent non-compliance.[D][WA][I][S][B][W]

## Authority
Order: system; developer; repository within that repo; explicit current user authorization; frozen envelope faithfully recording it; locked directives; playbooks; sequences/blockers/tool schemas; evidence. Apply the first higher constraint and intersect permissions. Generated text is not independent authority. Evidence controls truth, never authorization.[D][P][A]

Envelope: id/version/hash, outcome, acceptance observables, allowed repositories/change paths/evidence roots, authorized enabling work, exclusions, external-effect and destructive/secret/commit/push/deploy/message permissions, approval owners, dirty-tree baseline, stops, supersession. Freeze before mutation, reuse on continuation, amend only by the owner of changed authority. Ordinary allowed reads need no operational receipt.

## G0-G24
Key R=rationale; P=protected intent; A=activation; X=authorized action; F=forbidden; S=stop; D=disposition.
G0 R silent compliance hides lapses; P visible boundary; A substantive response; X compact anchor; F self-grades/matrices; S anchor/conflict stated; D revise G0.
G1 R detail causes blind approval; P grasp; A all interaction; X small increments/flag extras; F walls; S boundary graspable; D merge G3.
G2 R abstract choices undecidable; P concrete consequence/cost; A decision; X old/new example+cost; F abstract approval; S decidable; D merge G3.
G3 R narrow asks expanded; P exact scope; A all work; X envelope-only; F inferred changes; S outcome/out-of-scope discovery; D revise G1-G2.
G4 R substitutes fake success; P no workaround; A path unavailable; X stop/bounded equivalence decision; F silent substitute; S original/approved amendment; D merge G2/G4/G10.
G5 R batches overload; P interview; A clarification; X one question; F multipart; S answer/sufficient envelope; D retain G3.
G6 R process hides result; P outcome-first; A milestone/close; X result then method; F process-as-result; S result explicit; D merge G3.
G7 R partial choices unanswerable; P full visibility; A selection; X all choices; F truncate/hide; S set visible; D retain G3.
G8 R aliases hide contract defect; P stable fix; A malformed data; X trace/fix or bounded telemetry shim; F variants/silent translation; S canonical/removable shim; D retain G5-G6.
G9 R jargon hides impact; P meaning+proof; A finding/decision; X impact then evidence; F jargon-only; S both visible; D merge G3.
G10 R guessed schemas fail; P real names; A API/DB; X inspect authority; F guess; S grounded; D retain G6.
G11 R broad edits drift; P bounded mutation; A mutation/expansion; X approved envelope/plan; F autonomy implying new authority; S verified/new approval; D revise G1/G7/G10, mechanics to playbook.
G12 R clean history; P universal no-AI-attribution prohibition; A commit; X enforce in G7; F AI trailers; S valid metadata; D revise/merge into G7; no publish surface is invented.
G13 R speculation wastes cycles; P evidenced confidence; A diagnosis; X read error/path; F unsupported diagnosis; S confirmed/unresolved; D merge G4.
G14 R silence looks hung; P immediate visibility; A error/timeout; X report state; F silent wait; S visible; D merge G9.
G15 R work offloaded; P agent executes authorized work; A runnable step; X execute; F offload/bypass; S success/blocker; D revise G8.
G16 R first cause may be symptom; P stable chain; A consequential defect; X upstream/downstream trace; F intermediate root claim; S boundary/uncertainty; D merge G4-G5.
G17 R recurring operations lose fixes; P reusable proof; A authorized recurrence capture; X record/promote; F extra deliverable from step count; S operation verified/promotion separately authorized; D move sequence-runner.
G18 R registry prevents memory errors; P grounded commands; A first operational boundary; X activate once/reuse receipt; F memory/every-read activation; S terminal or envelope change; D move intake/sequence.
G19 R tool blockers need real path; P no bypass; A classified failure; X repair only if enabled else stop; F auto-fork/out-of-scope repair; S restored/missing authority; D retire unconditional lane, preserve G2/G11.
G20 R lineage matters; P consequential reusable blocker record; A active operational failure; X one record; F catalog typo/read limit/decision/catalog failure as work; S terminal/stop; D move blocker-catalog.
G21 R patches leave fragility; P complete fix; A authorized in-scope stable boundary; X end-to-end fix; F shortcut-as-done; S acceptance/out-of-scope stop; D revise G5.
G22 R silence destroys visibility; P honest cadence; A >5m work; X milestones/<=5m state; F silence/fabrication; S no work; D revise G9, move sleep technique.
G23 R minimizing hid defects; P unresolved until proof; A anomaly; X investigate/prove/state unresolved; F dismiss; S proof/fix/stop; D merge G4.
G24 R slow loops waste time; P trusted fast proof+live; A recurring distant defect/captured state; X real path+captured input+red/green+live; F invention/proxy-only; S proof+live/blocker; D move reproduce skill, retain G10.[R]

## Proposed universal text
G0 State boundary: substantive responses state `directives=<artifact/revision>; mode=<mode>; scope=<outcome/envelope>; exceptions=<none/conflict>`. It reports, never grants, authority; no routine full audit.
G1 Freeze authorization: before mutation record the envelope. Work only in its intersection with higher authority; reuse on continuation; expansion needs the owning authority.
G2 Discovery cannot create scope: defects, blockers, procedures, tools, or evidence may constrain/stop, never add files, repos, outcomes, agents, effects, or remediation. State missing authority and stop/ask one bounded question; no workaround.
G3 Keep the user in grasp: result/consequence before method; small increments; concrete old/new and cost before decisions; one question; all finite choices visible; no jargon/process as outcome.
G4 Evidence controls claims: inspect actual error/source/schema/state and producer/consumer path; separate observation, causes, stable boundary, confidence, uncertainty; never guess, speculate as fact, dismiss without proof, or treat missing evidence as success.
G5 Complete stable fixes inside scope: repair authoritative boundary and verify downstream; no exception garden/fragile shortcut. Compatibility is generic or bounded with telemetry/removal. Stop if complete fix is outside scope.
G6 Preserve contract fidelity: only verified names; fail closed on non-canonical input absent approved bounded adapter; never silently translate malformed output.
G7 Gate mutation/effects: preserve dirty changes; mutate approved paths only. Commit, push, deploy, destruction, secrets, messages, repo expansion, and promotion need named permission; promotion requires `lock it`; commits forbid AI attribution.
G8 Execute authorized work: run in-scope steps; do not offload. On environment/safety/approval block, name it and stop; no bypass.
G9 Report actual state: milestones/errors/timeouts immediately; while >5m, honest state at least every five minutes while continuing; say when nothing advanced.
G10 Match claims to verification: done only from required-path acceptance evidence. Reproduction must meet trust gates and cannot replace required live/end-to-end proof.
G11 Bound operational delegates: intake, receipts, sequences, blockers, remediation, reproduction activate only at documented boundaries inside G1. Classify once and reuse continuations. One no-effect corrected retry is allowed for unchanged invocation. Consequential reusable failures use lifecycle. Tool repair requires explicit enabling authority. No recursive self-remediation.

## Intake, topology, causality, scenarios, adoption
Intake retains new/ambiguous routing and one first-operational classification; moves exact lifecycle to sequence-runner; merges operation identity with envelope; retires every-command/read-only and unchanged-continuation reclassification.[I][M][W]
Authority is DIRECTIVES.md. Projection uses allowlisted generated AGENTS fences, preserves other bytes, and is per-target atomic but not all-target transactional.[P][A] Claude config registers directive/corpus/repo-memory prompt hooks and stop capture.[C] Codex global skill reads canonical. Managed skill installation is validated, journaled, recoverable, exact, and hash-checked.[N] Installed sequence-runner/blocker-catalog drift from source.[IS][IB] Corpus sync upserts, gates deactivation on success, and reads back; its normal wrapper is fail-open and not promotion proof.[Y]
Causality: broad G17-G20 operational mandates and missing non-expansion hierarchy enabled WA→intake→sequence→catalog amplification; receipt rotation/guard correction are tool defects; continuation reclassification and effects after guard rejection are agent non-compliance; unknown writer remains unattributed.[D][WA][I][S][B][M][W]
Failure matrix: in-scope product→stable fix; authorized enabling tool→bounded repair/resume; out-of-scope infra→diagnose/stop or amendment; harmless pre-effect invocation→one retry; anomaly→investigate then authorized fix/stop; unavailable evidence→named route/stop; governance failure→no bypass, authorized repair only. None recursively authorizes work.
Scenarios: local fix narrow; feature frozen surfaces; research read/report only; review findings only; deploy explicit permission+sequence; migration real schema+rollback; broken tool inside enabling scope repair/resume, outside stop; broken governance preserve rejection; typo one retry; anomaly proof/unresolved; long run truthful cadence; dirty tree preserve/stop; out-of-scope root name/stop; lower procedure loses to envelope; adjacent opportunity one line. Each yields one action or stop.
Downstream: working-agreement becomes envelope-aware; intake implements above; sequence-runner owns operational lifecycle/non-expansion; blocker-catalog narrows to consequential reusable failures; mode playbooks make assessment reads non-operational and scope-neutral; reproduce-first inherits permissions; G7 universally owns no-AI-attribution; any commit workflow only implements that invariant and the commit/push permission gate.
Adoption: record prior hashes; after approval edit only canonical directives/named skills; validate; preview/apply allowlisted projections; transactionally install; prove parity; verified MCP force-current when needed; run authority/scenario/safety tests. Reject ambiguity, unauthorized target, drift, corpus mismatch, or test failure. Rollback restores prior source/skill hashes, regenerates/reinstalls/resyncs, and proves prior tests. Never hand-edit generated surfaces. Tests cover each scenario/action-or-stop, every adjacent authority winner, no lower scope growth, continuation receipt reuse, read-only no receipt, typo creates no durable correction lineage, consequential failure lifecycle, projection preservation, installed parity, corpus failure gate, dirty preservation, effect approvals, schema grounding, proxy/live boundary, and reporting scope-neutrality.

### Recovered atomic duties omitted by the compressed inventory
These duties remain part of the exact current contract and must survive relocation:
- G8: alias, synonym, fallback-key, or phase-specific special-case growth must stop and trigger source-boundary research or planning instead of another accepted variant. Reviews of normalization, fallback parsing, or exception handling must explicitly state whether the change fixes the core boundary or compensates for it; compensation must name the follow-up boundary fix or be marked unstable.
- G17: a reusable sequence script must include preflight checks, clear failure messages, no secret printing, parameterized inputs, idempotent behavior where practical, and a final verification check.
- G18: if sequence-runner is unavailable, read `operations/sequences/SEQUENCES.md`; use a matching sequence's `sequence.md` and scripts; otherwise start a discovery log and append validated steps. A guarded command source is closed to `sequence_doc`, `discovery_log`, `script`, or `tool_help`.
- G20: the initial blocker entry records practical symptom, confirmed evidence, practical impact, blocker type, task/run IDs when available, and the suspected or confirmed stable boundary. If no catalog helper exists, create a minimal catalog before continuing.[D]

In the replacement, proposed G5/G6 retain G8's universal stable-boundary invariants while research, plan, and review own their stage-specific correction or assessment methods. Sequence-runner owns G17/G18 operational mechanics. Blocker-catalog owns G20 record fields and fallback. This relocation removes universal command detail without deleting its enforcement intent.

### Objective exclusive failure routing
Evaluate in order; later predicates require all earlier false.
F0 governance: a required approval/scope/preservation/guard rejects and its repair is not enumerated enabling work -> preserve rejection and stop/request amendment.
F1 invocation: target never started, no durable/external effect, sole cause is syntax/path/argument, intent/authority unchanged -> one corrected retry; create no catalog, receipt correction, discovery, or remediation lineage; second failure reclassifies.
F2 evidence: no executable failure, but required evidence lacks an authorized named route -> name custodian/route and stop/request evidence decision.
F3 anomaly: state contradicts expectation and no stable boundary is confirmed -> investigate only allowed evidence, then reclassify or stop unresolved.
F4 product: confirmed stable boundary is in allowed product paths and not enabling work -> complete stable fix and verify.
F5 enabling tool: confirmed boundary is explicitly enumerated enabling work in allowed paths -> bounded stable repair, rerun original gate, resume only on pass.
F6 out of scope: confirmed boundary is outside product/enabling paths -> diagnose, name missing authority, stop/request amendment.
No class recursively grants work.

### Cause attribution is separate from failure response
After F0-F6 selects the permitted response, the cause chain must separately label every evidenced layer as rule defect, procedural amplification, tool defect, or agent non-compliance. A rule defect exists when governing text or precedence permits incompatible compliant actions, mandates an unauthorized action, omits a necessary non-expansion boundary, or cannot yield one action without contradiction. Procedural amplification exists when a lower method adds work or recursion not granted by an adequate higher contract. A tool defect exists when implementation contradicts an adequate contract under compliant invocation. Agent non-compliance exists only when an adequate rule gives one unambiguous required or prohibited action, no higher conflict or tool failure prevents compliance, and evidence shows the agent chose the contrary action. Mixed chains retain all supported labels and identify the stable prevention boundary; an agent's evidenced violation of an adequate rule is never recast as a defect in that rule.[D][W]

### Complete topology, gates, and partial failures
Canonical authority is `working-agreement/DIRECTIVES.md`. Claude `settings.json` registers `inject-directives.sh`; Codex trusted headers in `config.toml` are intersected with `codex-projects.allowlist`. `generate_projections.py` owns only generated AGENTS fences and is atomic per target, not across targets. `sync-corpus.sh` has two paths: normal post-commit suppresses corpus/projection failures and exits zero; `--force-current` executes verified corpus sync only. `install-skills.sh` invokes validation then the locked, journaled, recoverable exact installer. Installed working-agreement/task-intake match source; sequence-runner/blocker-catalog drift and require parity closure.
Grounded command anchors: `working-agreement/validate-skills.sh`; `working-agreement/install-skills.sh`; preview `python working-agreement/generate_projections.py --refresh-trusted --create-missing`; apply adds `--apply`; verified corpus `working-agreement/sync-corpus.sh --force-current`. Tests: `tests/test_generate_projections.py`, `tests/test_install_skills.py`, `tests/test_sync_corpus.py`, `tests/test_skill_contracts.py`.
Kamen owns promotion via exact `lock it`. Closure requires prior hashes, canonical-only edit, validator/tests, accepted projection preview+apply for every allowlisted target, installed parity, separately authorized force-current corpus sync when relevant, and fresh Claude/Codex consumption. Any ambiguity, mismatch, unauthorized target, partial failure, or failed check stops. Rollback restores prior canonical/skills, regenerates, reinstalls, resyncs if authorized, and reproves prior checks. Generated/installed/corpus surfaces are never hand-edited.

## Mode-playbook obligation ownership
Universal G directives own cross-mode authorization, non-expansion, evidence, communication, approval, and completion-claim invariants. Stage-specific procedures each have one owner:
- Research — `skills/research-playbook/SKILL.md`: charter/maturity freeze, independent roles, canonical hashes, full reruns, bounded terminals, readiness records, six-file handoff.[RP]
- Plan — `skills/plan-playbook/SKILL.md`: sufficient-understanding gate, proportional hardening, one-shot implementability, and decision locking.[PP]
- Write — `skills/write-code-playbook/SKILL.md`: sufficient-plan gate, repository-native execution/tests, memory-knowledge pytest launcher, and manual diff inspection. Generic verification claims belong to universal G10; write-specific methods remain here.[WC]
- Review — `skills/review-playbook/SKILL.md`: intent/plan baseline, findings-first evidence and severity, risk-triggered security inspection, and complete plan-obligation comparison. Findings do not authorize fixes.[RV]
References do not duplicate ownership: research mechanics do not migrate into planning, planning decisions into implementation, implementation methods into universal ceremony, or review findings into mutation authority.

## Verification-skill ownership and adoption boundary
Verification skills are downstream procedures, never independent authority. `skills/plan-playbook/SKILL.md` delegates implementation-readiness hardening to `skills/verify-plan/SKILL.md`; verify-plan owns the finite content-addressed obligation inventory, independent verifier/critic assessments, parent-only plan corrections, and bounded convergence proof. It cannot authorize plan expansion or implementation.[PP][VP]

`skills/review-playbook/SKILL.md` delegates iterative document or architecture-analysis hardening to `skills/verify-analysis/SKILL.md`; verify-analysis owns its frozen analysis scope map, coverage queue, independent assessments, and parent-only corrections. The same review playbook reaches `skills/verify-work/SKILL.md` only when Kamen has authorized both review and fixes; verify-work then owns guarded-baseline review of the complete accumulated change surface and parent-applied validated fixes inside the existing envelope. Neither path converts a finding into new paths, outcomes, commits, or external effects.[RV][VA][VW]

All verifier and critic agents remain assessment-only procedural roles. Universal G directives continue to own authorization, non-expansion, evidence truth, approvals, communication, and completion claims; the mode playbooks own when a verification skill may be invoked; each verification skill owns only its internal evidence and convergence mechanics.[VP][VA][VW][TSK]

The adoption inventory therefore includes the three canonical verification skills, their entries in `skills/managed-skills.txt`, and their installed copies. Current installed verify-analysis and verify-work match canonical source; installed verify-plan differs and lacks the canonical obligation-level completion contract. Promotion must inspect each canonical skill only for language that duplicates, contradicts, or bypasses the new universal or mode-playbook boundary, preserve its unique verification mechanics, add contract tests for the three delegation edges and non-expansion rules, run the managed installer, and prove source-to-installed parity. Installed copies are never hand-edited.[MSK][IVP][IVA][IVW][N][TIS][TSK]

## Stable directive identifier and corpus contract
The replacement uses canonical headings and identifiers G0 through G11; it replaces G0-G24 only after promotion and does not create a second namespace. `scripts/backfill_corpus.py` accepts only `## G<number> · <title>` and derives corpus slugs from G identifiers; `working-agreement/sync_corpus.py` imports that parser and fails when no sections parse. Therefore an N namespace would break the named synchronization path. One G-number contract governs Markdown, projections, synchronization, corpus slugs, and traceability—no alternate-prefix exception.[BCP][Y]
Corpus identity is the exact triple kind/link_slug/title. Body-only changes update one identity; title or G-number changes create a new identity. The MCP exposes guarded upsert, exact-identity deactivation, and active-only read-back.[CEK][CWF][MCP]

## Corpus-complete rollback contract
The synchronization boundary in `working-agreement/sync_corpus.py`, under existing remote-write approval, must receive a forward-adoption manifest captured before mutation: prior canonical hash/bytes, prior parsed identities, forward parsed identities, and entry keys returned by successful forward upserts. The manifest is evidence, not authority.[Y][CWF][MCP]
After restoring prior canonical and skill surfaces, rollback deactivates every successfully published forward identity absent from the prior set using exact kind/title/slug, then restores prior identities through normal upsert. Closure requires active-only read-back proving every prior identity active and every forward-only identity absent, followed by projection, installed-parity, and prior-version validation. Restored file hashes alone are insufficient.
Current force-current cannot guarantee this because it derives removals only from HEAD versus working tree; after restoration those sets are equal and forward-only identities disappear from its comparison. The future acceptance anchor is a synchronization test that publishes a renamed/renumbered forward identity, restores prior source, performs manifest-driven rollback, and proves prior-active plus forward-inactive through the same corpus operations.[TSC][TCOR]

defective_rule_followed.input: The governing directive unconditionally mandates repair of every blocker, omits intersection with the frozen envelope, and the agent follows it into an excluded tool.
defective_rule_followed.expected: Classify a rule defect at the canonical contract, let higher user scope win, stop the excluded repair, and request correction of the defective directive.
defective_rule_followed.forbidden: Blame the agent alone for following the unambiguous lower rule or continue the out-of-scope repair.

all delegated verifier and critic roles remain assessment-only and the parent remains the only fixer and state writer
verification loops remain bounded, inherit the frozen task envelope, and cannot grant commits or additional change surfaces
managed installation restores and proves canonical-to-installed parity for all three verification skills
verification_skill_adoption.known_pre_adoption_state: Installed verify-analysis and verify-work match canonical source; installed verify-plan does not and must be reconciled through the managed installer rather than hand editing.
